vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: furry-art-skill
Version: 1.1.0

The skill is a functional utility for generating images via the Neta AI (TalesofAI) API. The `furryart.js` script handles argument parsing, API token resolution, and task polling as described in the documentation. While the script contains minor implementation flaws (calling an undefined `readEnvFile` function and using unexpanded tilde paths for configuration files), these are unintentional bugs rather than malicious features. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or prompt injection attempts.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated purpose (generating images via the Neta API) but contains inconsistencies and undocumented behavior (attempts to read local .env files, mismatched env-var names, and an undefined helper) that warrant caution before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the implementation: the script calls the Neta/TalesofAI endpoints and requires a NETA token. Requesting a NETA_TOKEN is proportional to the stated purpose. However, the code also looks for token data in specific local .env paths (~/.openclaw/workspace/.env and ~/developer/clawhouse/.env) which is beyond the single env-var model the SKILL.md describes and suggests tighter coupling to local Claw workspaces.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs only to provide NETA_TOKEN or --token. The JS code tries additional token-resolution fallbacks by reading two specific files in the user's home directory (those paths are not documented in SKILL.md/README). That is scope creep: the runtime will attempt to read local files for credentials. Additionally, the README mentions NETA_API_BASE_URL while the code reads NETA_API_URL (env-var name mismatch), and the code references a readEnvFile() helper that is not present in the distributed file — this is either a bug or an obfuscated omission. These issues mean the skill may behave differently than documented and could access local files unexpectedly.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; the package is instruction + a single JS script and package.json. There are no downloads or external installers performed by the skill itself, which is the lower-risk model for skills.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only NETA_TOKEN is declared as required in package.json and SKILL.md. The code also optionally uses an API base env var and the undocumented fallback file reads to obtain a token. The number of credentials requested is reasonable for the stated purpose, but the undocumented fallback to local .env files increases the surface for accidental token disclosure. The mismatch of env var names (README mentions NETA_API_BASE_URL, code uses NETA_API_URL) can lead to confusion and misconfiguration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent or system-wide privileges, is not always-enabled, and does not modify other skill or agent configurations. It only runs when invoked.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims (call Neta to generate images) but has some red flags and rough edges: 1) The JS tries to read NETA_TOKEN from two hard-coded dotfile locations in your home directory — these fallbacks are not documented in SKILL.md and could cause the script to read files you didn't expect. 2) The README and code use different env-var names for the API base (NETA_API_BASE_URL vs NETA_API_URL), and the code calls a readEnvFile() function that isn't included (likely a bug). Before installing or running: prefer passing --token on the command line or explicitly set NETA_TOKEN in the environment; inspect/patch the furryart.js source (or reject the skill) to remove or control the fallback file reads; verify the token is scoped/limited (you may want a throwaway or limited-permission token); run in an isolated environment if you must test; contact the publisher for clarification or a corrected release. If you cannot confirm the missing helper and file-read behavior, treat the skill as risky for exposing your NETA token.
